description: The forwarded request target is percent-encoded from the received bytes exactly once (MCPWARP.md §4.3): a raw UTF-8 query `?q=café` (bytes 63 61 66 C3 A9) reaches the handler as `?q=caf%C3%A9`, uppercase hex, never double-encoded as `caf%C3%83%C2%A9` (the bytes read as latin1 and encoded again).
in:
POST /mcp?q=café HTTP/1.1
Host: notes-tester.mcpwarp.test
accept: application/json, text/event-stream
content-type: application/json
user-agent: Go-http-client/1.1
Content-Length: 40

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping"}
out:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/json
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

28
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping"}
0
notes: The `in` text is written to the stream as UTF-8, so `é` is the two bytes C3 A9. Compare upstream.url byte for byte: a runtime URL object must not decode the escape or re-encode the raw bytes.
